notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — three P0 correctness issues (slow-path validity error variant regression, AiaError::MalformedCertificate misuse, broken README examples) and six P1 architectural lock-ins that need resolution before 1.0. All P0 issues have clear fixes; the P1 lock-ins (AIA fetcher in use-case wrappers, custom SignatureVerifier in wrappers, URI scheme filter location) require API decisions while breaking changes are still free.
Confidence: ~70% chance of a missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-sqek.1 (slow-path validity error regression — I traced the code paths but did not run a probe to confirm the exact error variant observed in the AIA-slow-path-+-expired-leaf scenario; the bd issue describes what would happen per code reading, but only a test run could confirm). Uncertainty driven by: (a) the pkix-path-builder internals (build_first_valid_path's exact handling of validate_path errors) — I read the Error enum but not the full iteration logic; (b) whether last_aia_error capture interacts correctly when batch_fetch returns mixed success/failure across multiple URIs (no test exercises this — every existing test uses single-URI scenarios). Would raise confidence if: a probe test with chain=[expired_leaf_with_AIA_URI] under a working AiaFetcher and now_unix=0 confirmed PKIX-sqek.1; a probe test with two AIA URIs (one returning a usable cert, the other returning garbage) confirmed which is surfaced. These probes are filed implicitly via the P0 issue descriptions; /do-beads can write them.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — five P1 contract lock-ins (Verifier generics shape, error-type leakage, wrapper-chain[0] panic dependency, broad pub-use module re-exports, plus PKIX-sqek.4/.20 wrapper signature lock-in) need a unified shape decision before 1.0; cost of getting them wrong is a major-version migration for every downstream consumer.
API contract confidence: ~75% chance of a missed contract issue. Least confident flags: PKIX-sqek.21 (chain[0] panic dependency — I read pkix-path:1561 confirming the empty-chain gate exists today, but did not write a probe that injects an empty chain and observes the actual surfaced error; only confirmed via code reading); PKIX-sqek.22 (verify_batch 'sequential' wording lock-in — I have not surveyed downstream code in the workspace that observes batch-order side effects, so the lock-in cost is hypothetical). Uncertainty driven by: (a) I did not enumerate cross-crate symbol re-exports for the 'self' module re-exports (PKIX-sqek.25) — there may be additional pkix_chain::pkix_X::Y symbols that consumers depend on in ways the rustdoc doesn't surface; (b) the serde wire format coupling (PKIX-sqek.26) — I read the feature-gating but did not generate a sample serialized Error to check whether upstream enum representations are tagged or untagged, which determines forward-compat behavior; (c) I did not test cargo doc to confirm that the [] cross-references in verify_chain_default (PKIX-sqek.32) actually resolve to the misleading paths I claim — they may render correctly even with misleading prose. Would raise confidence if: a probe ran cargo public-api or cargo semver-checks against the diff window to enumerate symbol additions; a probe wrote a downstream consumer that explicitly pattern-matches on Error::Path's inner pkix_path::Error variants to confirm PKIX-sqek.27's match-arm cost; a probe ran cargo doc --all-features and inspected the rendered HTML to confirm the cross-reference accuracy claims.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — pkix-chain is largely idiomatic modern Rust (combinators, ? operator, derived traits, matches! macro, is_some_and). Eight Rust-idiom findings filed (PKIX-sqek.34-41), no unsafe, no Box<dyn Error>, no unwrap/expect outside tests. Five P1 findings are mechanical fixes (UFCS dance, stdlib reinvention, C-STRUCT-BOUNDS violation, index-arithmetic loop, nested if-let); three P2 findings are stylistic cleanups (static_assertions, Cow FQ paths, duplicated ok_or). The trait-bounds-on-struct issue (PKIX-sqek.36) is the most substantive — it has a named Rust API guideline citation and is a Cargo.toml-shaped maintenance burden going forward. No idiom finding rises to the architectural-redesign level; all are local edits within the existing file structure.
Rust idiom confidence: ~80% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: PKIX-sqek.37 (static_assertions adoption — the hand-rolled const _: fn() pattern *works* and adds zero dependencies; the engineering case is real but mild, this could plausibly be argued as taste; the workspace's review-rusty prompt explicitly encourages static_assertions, which moves it from opinion into 'flag this'). Uncertainty driven by: (a) I did not run cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets to enumerate every lint clippy would flag — the systematic candidates are likely a superset of what I caught by reading; specifically collapsible_if, redundant_closure_for_method_calls, needless_return, manual_strip and similar would surface mechanically; (b) I did not check whether the workspace-level Cargo.toml denies any clippy lints that would have caught my findings already (if cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes, the file is partially clippy-clean and my P1 findings are things clippy doesn't see by default); (c) I did not survey whether the test files (verify_*.rs, hostname_corpus.rs, mailbox_corpus.rs, serde_round_trip.rs) themselves contain non-idiomatic Rust — test code was deliberately excluded per the prompt's focus on production code idioms, but a serious Rust reviewer would also flag if test helpers reach for unwrap_or_else when ok_or_else suffices. Would raise confidence if: cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets ran and produced a delta against my findings; cargo fmt --check ran and confirmed no formatting drift beyond what review-myoss already pinned.
